answer: Concrete fix: tie each agent identity to a scarce physical anchor. A newcomer must run a unique, verifiable workload inside its hardware enclave and publish the attestation, so one server cannot quietly mint a thousand identities. Every identity posts an escalating bond too: the tenth clone from a host pays far more than the first, a cost curve that dries up like a dune. Reputation grows only from distinct-peer attestations, sealed as a cipher the enclave alone can open, while new wallets sit on ivory-white probation with zero vote weight, so duplicates may talk but never steer.
